claim: Borough Market in Southwark is home to over 100 independent traders and operates Tuesday-Sunday, closed Mondays.
quote: The market is home to over 100 independent traders, and Borough Market operates six days a week, typically closing on Mondays, from 10am to 5pm Tuesday to Friday, with Saturday opening at 9am and Sunday from 10am to 4pm.

claim: Borough Market's 2026 trend list flags South American (Venezuelan/Argentine) traders like La Pepia for arepas and Japanese-baking influences as things to look for in 2026.
quote: There has been an increased interest in South American cuisines, such as Venezuelan, Argentine and wider Latin American food, with Borough Market stalls like La Pepia offering arepas made by hand using responsibly sourced British ingredients

claim: Columbia Road Flower Market is a Sunday-only event in East London open 8am-3pm, transforming the narrow street into a wall of cut flowers and plants.
quote: On Sundays, Columbia Road transforms into a blooming wonderland with vendors lining the narrow street, selling fresh-cut flowers, plants, herbs, and more.

claim: Maltby Street Market in Bermondsey runs under 19th-century railway arches on Saturdays 10am-5pm and Sundays 11am-4pm and sits on the Bermondsey Beer Mile.
quote: Maltby Street Market is open Saturdays from 10am to 5pm and Sundays from 11am to 4pm. Additionally, Street Food Fridays return from 1 May 2026, from 5.30pm to 9pm.

claim: Broadway Market in Hackney runs every Saturday 9am-5pm with global street food (Thai, Ethiopian, tacos), sourdough from Pavilion Bakery, and pubs like the Cat and Mutton.
quote: Broadway Market is open from 9am to 5pm every Saturday.

claim: Brick Lane Market runs Sundays 10am-6pm with vintage clothing, the Boiler House food hall, street art, Beigel Bake and the curry houses of Banglatown.
quote: The Brick Lane Market operates every Sunday from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

claim: Old Spitalfields, next to Brick Lane, hosts themed days through the week including the Sunday Upmarket combining fashion, art and food.
quote: Sunday Upmarket combines fashion, art and food on Sundays, Backyard Market focuses on independent designers and runs on Saturdays and Sundays, and Boiler House Food brings together street food traders on weekends.

claim: Portobello Road in Notting Hill is the world's largest antiques market, stretching about two miles with 1,500+ dealers, busiest on Saturday 8:30am-4pm.
quote: Portobello Road Market is a massive open-air antiques market stretching over two miles throughout London's West End, the largest of its kind in the world, with over 1,500 dealers

claim: Saturday is Portobello's main antiques trading day with antique stalls concentrated between Portobello Road and Kensington Park Road; arrive before 11:30am to dodge crowds.
quote: Saturday tends to be the busiest day (as it is the main antiques trading day) and is packed full of tourists and street performers.

claim: Camden Market still tops 2026 food-market rankings with over 100 stalls spanning punk/vintage clothing, vegan eats and global street food.
quote: Camden Market is still one of London's most visited spots with over 100 stalls and shops in the area.

claim: Brixton Village and Market Row are covered Victorian arcades whose food reflects Caribbean heritage with Latin American and African influences alongside independent record and vintage shops.
quote: Brixton Village and Market Row have gained particular recognition for their food offerings reflecting the area's rich Caribbean heritage alongside influences from Latin America, Africa, and beyond

claim: Hampstead is a preserved village quarter of narrow lanes, historic pubs and art studios adjacent to Hampstead Heath, with planning rules that keep neon signs out.
quote: London neighbourhoods don't come more charming than Hampstead, its quaint village is full of cute shops, cafes and art studios.

claim: Shoreditch retains a creative edge in its bars, music venues and restaurants despite the fading of hipster-era trends, while Soho is the maze of nightlife, record shops and indie boutiques in central London.
quote: Once the home of the hipster... the subcultural cool kids may be few and far between nowadays, but you'll still find a creative edge in many of the bars, music venues and restaurants here.

claim: The Queen's Walk along South Bank links the London Eye, Southbank Centre, National Theatre, BFI, Tate Modern and Shakespeare's Globe in a flat 4km pedestrian stretch.
quote: The Jubilee Walkway is the South Bank's star path, where you'll tick off icons including Canary Wharf's towers, Tower Bridge, Shakespeare's Globe, Tate Modern, St Paul's, the Houses of Parliament, Big Ben, the London Eye, and City Hall.

claim: Greenwich is a UNESCO World Heritage Site whose walkable core links the Cutty Sark clipper, Greenwich Market, the Old Royal Naval College and the Royal Observatory atop the park.
quote: The historic tea clipper Cutty Sark is the fastest ship of its time and now a famous sight in the heart of Greenwich's UNESCO World Heritage Site.

claim: Greenwich Market is an undercover market with 120+ stalls, dedicated to antiques and collectables Tue/Thu/Fri and craft and design Wed/Fri/Sat/Sun.
quote: Greenwich Market showcases antiques and collectables Tuesday, Thursday and Friday and craft and design on Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday.
